analysis.evidence: הַבְּהֵמָה הַטְּהוֹרָה denotes clean animals collectively. The repeated שִׁבְעָה שִׁבְעָה assigns a count to each kind, giving כֹּל distributive force.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun with prefixed מִן. The נ assimilates to the following כ, producing מִכֹּל.

analysis.evidence: The agreeing adjective הַטְּהוֹרָה gives מִכֹּל הַבְּהֵמָה הַטְּהוֹרָה the sense “from among all the clean animals.” The verse repeats הַבְּהֵמָה for the unclean group, so the noun names the animals and the modifier specifies their ritual status.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ prefixed to a feminine singular absolute common noun, used collectively.

analysis.evidence: הַטְּהוֹרָה agrees with הַבְּהֵמָה in gender, number, and definiteness. The verse contrasts the clean animals taken by sevens with those described as לֹא טְהֹרָה, taken by twos.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ prefixed to a feminine singular absolute adjective modifying הַבְּהֵמָה.

analysis.evidence: Noah is told how many animals to take from each group. The following לְךָ means “for yourself” and identifies Noah as the one for whom the animals are taken.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, second person masculine singular, used as a command. The ת־ prefix marks the subject.

analysis.evidence: The marked שִׁבְעָה is the first numeral in שִׁבְעָה שִׁבְעָה. Repetition gives the count distributive force for each kind of clean animal. The parallel instruction uses שְׁנַיִם (“two”) for unclean animals.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute form of the cardinal numeral, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The marked שִׁבְעָה repeats the preceding שִׁבְעָה. Together they mean “by sevens” for the clean animals. The parallel instruction uses שְׁנַיִם “two” for the unclean animals, and both counts are followed by אִישׁ וְאִשְׁתּוֹ “a male and its mate.”
analysis.morphology: Cardinal numeral, masculine singular absolute, the second numeral in a distributive repetition.

analysis.evidence: הַבְּהֵמָה הַטְּהוֹרָה identifies the clean animals Noah is to take. In אִישׁ וְאִשְׁתּוֹ, “a male and its mate,” אִישׁ designates the male of each pair.
הַבְּהֵמָה הַטְּהוֹרָה identifies the animals Noah is to take. In אִישׁ וְאִשְׁתּוֹ, אִישׁ denotes the male, and the suffix וֹ refers back to it, identifying the female as its mate.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ + feminine singular construct noun אִשְׁתּ־ + third-person masculine singular possessive suffix וֹ.

draft.change: Add Genesis 7:2 as an example under the existing Hebrew partitive sense min-some-of in article min.
draft.definition: Introduces the whole from which a part or a number of members is selected.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 7:2, מִן introduces the unclean animals and שְׁנַיִם specifies how many to take from among them.

analysis.evidence: In וּמִן הַבְּהֵמָה אֲשֶׁר לֹא טְהֹרָה הִוא, מִן introduces the group of animals that are unclean. שְׁנַיִם gives the number Noah is to take from that group, and אִישׁ וְאִשְׁתּוֹ identifies the two as a male and its mate.
analysis.morphology: Prefixed coordinating conjunction וּ־ (“and”) + preposition מִן in its full, unsuffixed form.
analysis.sense: Partitive, marking the group from which a specified number is taken.

analysis.evidence: The relative clause אֲשֶׁר לֹא טְהֹרָה הִוא identifies the animals that are unclean. They are to be taken in twos, male and female, in contrast to the clean animals mentioned earlier in the verse.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine singular absolute, with the prefixed definite article הַ־, used collectively.

analysis.evidence: אֲשֶׁר introduces the relative clause לֹא טְהֹרָה הִוא, “it is not clean.” The feminine singular pronoun הִוא refers back to הַבְּהֵמָה, giving “the animal that is not clean.”
analysis.morphology: Invariant relative particle without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In אֲשֶׁר לֹא טְהֹרָה הִוא, “which is not clean,” לֹא negates the predicate adjective טְהֹרָה. The relative clause distinguishes these animals from הַבְּהֵמָה הַטְּהוֹרָה, “the clean animals,” earlier in the verse.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected negative particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In אֲשֶׁר לֹא טְהֹרָה הִוא, “which is not clean,” טְהֹרָה agrees with הַבְּהֵמָה, “the animal.” The preceding לֹא negates the same adjective used in הַבְּהֵמָה הַטְּהוֹרָה, “the clean animal,” earlier in the verse.
analysis.morphology: Predicative adjective, feminine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In אֲשֶׁר לֹא טְהֹרָה הִוא, «which is not clean», הִוא is the subject of the relative clause. It refers back to the feminine singular הַבְּהֵמָה, «the animal», and טְהֹרָה is the predicate adjective.
analysis.morphology: Independent third-person feminine singular pronoun, written הִוא and read הִיא.

analysis.evidence: שְׁנַיִם gives the number of unclean animals to take. The following אִישׁ וְאִשְׁתּוֹ identifies the two as a male and its mate.
analysis.morphology: Masculine dual absolute cardinal numeral, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: שְׁנַיִם אִישׁ וְאִשְׁתּוֹ specifies the two unclean animals as a male and its mate. אִישׁ designates the male member of the pair.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The verse specifies two unclean animals (שְׁנַיִם). The phrase אִישׁ וְאִשְׁתּוֹ identifies the pair as a male and its female mate, with the suffix referring to the male.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ plus feminine singular construct noun אִשְׁתּ־ with third-person masculine singular possessive suffix וֹ.
